experiment.intervention: A byte-owning compiler/admission helper binds expected digest, engine compilation and static ABI inspection to the same immutable snapshot, returning only an admitted Module. Remove duplicate engine validate from Kernel.create; preserve standalone inspectKernelWasm.
experiment.target: Repeatable reduction in complete fresh Agent-command time, with all digest, size, invalid-WASM, ABI, no-start/import and caller-mutation checks preserved.
experiment.safety: Compilation may occur before ABI rejection, but instantiation must never occur until both validity and ABI checks pass. No module/proof parameter or validation bypass is accepted.

experiment.intervention: Weakly retain at most the most recently admitted immutable Module, keyed by its validated SHA-256. Recheck owned caller bytes and expected digest before every lookup. Each Kernel strongly holds its Module and creates fresh guest memory/identity/tokens. No Program, Session, reply or outcome cache.
experiment.law: Cache hits must be observationally equivalent to re-admitting the exact bytes; different or mutated bytes cannot reuse authority. Cache lifetime cannot keep code alive after all Kernel owners are gone.
experiment.guardrails: size/digest/ABI failures; caller mutation; distinct kernel outputs; fresh guest memory; collected-cache miss; unsupported WeakRef fallback; concurrent different digests
experiment.measurement: Report first/cold factory separately from repeated factories; preserve matched complete fresh-call results and acknowledge code reuse.

firstCall.method: First factory and invocation in independent new Node processes; imports/file reads before clock, no prior WASM compilation in each child.

qualification: Targeted captured Agent commands, exact output equality. Split compile/instantiate alone had no repeatable benefit. Single validation and weak code reuse improve repeated factory calls; first-call results remain separately reported. Full Agent macro remeasurement follows authenticated runtime repinning.
